title: How to animate your logo for Instagram and Reels
meta_title: Animate Your Logo for Reels: DIY vs Hire — Akdeinz Motion
description: Animate your logo for Instagram and Reels yourself with Canva, CapCut or Jitter, or hire it for €390 in 3 working days. Tools, steps, hours, costs.
answer: The quickest way to animate a logo for Instagram is a template in Canva or CapCut, which takes roughly 1–3 hours for a first version [VERIFY]. For a custom animation that matches your brand, you can hire it: Akdeinz Motion’s Logo Sting (3–6 s) is €390 excl. VAT, delivered in 3 working days in 16:9, 9:16 and 1:1, plus a transparent-background render.

diy.intro: Reels and Stories are vertical (9:16), so build the logo animation vertically first and export a square or landscape version afterwards. You need your logo as a vector file (SVG, AI or PDF) or a large PNG with a transparent background.

tools.name: Canva
tools.note: Easiest start. Animation presets on text, shapes and images; exports MP4. Limited control over timing and easing compared with a timeline tool [VERIFY].

tools.name: CapCut
tools.note: Phone and desktop editor with keyframes, templates and sound. Good for a simple logo reveal. Check the commercial-use terms of any template or music you use [VERIFY].

tools.name: Jitter
tools.note: Browser-based motion design tool made for short animations such as logo reveals; more control than a template without the learning curve of After Effects [VERIFY].

tools.name: After Effects
tools.note: Full control and the industry standard. A logo reveal is a good first project, but getting comfortable takes weeks (see the guide on learning After Effects).

steps: Get the logo as SVG or a high-resolution transparent PNG. A blurry logo cannot be fixed by animation.
Create a 1080 × 1920 px canvas (9:16). Make a 1080 × 1080 px copy for the feed.
Pick one idea: the logo slides in, builds from its shapes, or fades up with one accent movement. Keep it to 3–5 seconds.
Add a short sound: a soft hit or whoosh timed to the moment the logo lands. Use music or sound you have the right to use commercially.
Export as MP4, watch it on your phone with the sound on, then check it on a bright and a dark background.
Export the other ratios. An MP4 cannot carry a transparent background, so a see-through version needs a different export format [VERIFY].
diy.hours: Realistic time for a first logo animation: about 1–3 hours with a Canva or CapCut template, about 3–8 hours in Jitter including learning the tool, and 40+ hours before After Effects feels comfortable [VERIFY].

rows: Free tiers exist; paid plans vary [VERIFY]. The real cost is your time.

time_line: Learning to do this: ~1–3 hours with a template, 40+ hours for After Effects [VERIFY]. Akdeinz: €390, 3 days.

diy_fine.p: Doing it yourself is a fair choice in these cases:
ul: You post casually and a template look is fine.
The logo is simple (a wordmark or a single shape) and you only need a short fade or slide.
You have no budget this month and plenty of time.
You enjoy learning the tool and want to make many small variations yourself.
diy_fine.not_fine: It is worth hiring when the logo will open every ad and video for months, when it runs in paid ads, or when the hours you would spend are worth more than €390.

faq.q: How long should an animated logo be for Instagram Reels?
faq.a: Short. Akdeinz Motion’s Logo Sting is 3–6 seconds, which is long enough for one clear movement and a moment where the logo holds still.

faq.q: What does a logo animation cost?
faq.a: A Logo Sting (3–6 s) is €390 excl. VAT with a 3 working day turnaround. An extra revision round is €90, 4K is +20%, and rush delivery under 72 hours is +35%.

faq.q: Can I animate my logo for free?
faq.a: Yes. Canva and CapCut have free tiers [VERIFY]. The trade-off is your time and a look that many other accounts share.
Instagram-ready 1080p MP4 files in 16:9, 9:16 and 1:1. A Logo Sting also includes a transparent-background render for placing the logo over other footage.

faq.q: Do I get the project files?
faq.a: No. The deliverable is the rendered video file only.
